headline: Germany's transport minister says he wants Tesla's supervised driving software approved across the EU and that Germany could consider acting alone if that fails.
score_reason: Political support from a major EU government, but only a statement of intent and open technical and liability questions.
importance_line: Drivers in Germany and regulators across the EU are affected, but the minister himself named unresolved technical and liability issues and a decision is unlikely before December.
summary: heise online, citing the dpa news agency, reports that Transport Minister Steffen Bilger said at a Berlin conference on Tuesday that he wants Tesla's Full Self-Driving (Supervised) used across the EU soon, and that if EU agreement fails officials should discuss "what can be done in Germany". Heise adds that the Dutch regulator approved the system in April for the Netherlands only, Germany has not adopted it, and a decision on EU-wide approval is probably not due before December.
notes: Read via heise online because the Electric Vehicles page was blocked; the quote "what can be done in Germany" is a paraphrase rendering of heise’s English text.
